newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's VAW defends EU aluminium import tariff.
newsitem.headline: Germany's VAW defends EU aluminium import tariff.

text.p: Attacks on the European Union's six percent import tariff on primary aluminium were unjustified and self-seeking, Karl Wobbe, board member at Germany's VAW aluminium AG, said in a telephone interview on Tuesday.
"The latest GATT round agreed on keeping the present tariff structure, with built-in reductions up to the year 2000," he said.
"The EU Commission, knowing about the European aluminium industry's disadvantages, helped safeguard its interests."
VAW is a unit of utility group Viag AG.
Wobbe singled out Alcan Aluminium Ltd among the opponents of the tariff, along with several U.S. producers, South Africa's Alusaf, which is a unit of Gencor Ltd, and Dubai Aluminium Co.
He said Alcan unsuccessfully tried to get the issue debated at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) meeting in Singapore later on this month via its British subsidiary.

"But they are Canadian and wish to import aluminium here... they also don't mention that the North American market has lots of non-tariff barriers such as anti-dumping laws which distort world trade far more than our modest tariffs," he said.
Opponents say the tariff is protectionist and discriminatory because it only applies to some countries.

But Wobbe said the majority of European producers wanted the tariff to stay to compensate them for high energy and environmental costs and competiton arising from the influx of cheap former USSR metal into Europe.

Processors supporting abolition in the hope of securing cheap raw materials should realise that once the tariff was eliminated, tariffs on aluminium semis imports of 8.5 percent might also need to go.
This would open the floodgates to aluminium product imports.
